leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Approve accountable executive mandates and escalation authority for priority remediation.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: 4 linked finding(s) and 4 consolidated risk(s) drive this decision.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: Hard-gate, governance and maturity-limiting controls require authority to allocate resources and resolve blockers.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Name one accountable executive per linked control and approve a 30-day escalation route.
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Priority controls remain ownerless or blocked and the maturity reading remains constrained.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: Signed mandate with decision rights, owners and escalation cadence.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Choose and record remediation rather than passive acceptance for Critical and High risks.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: 4 linked finding(s) and 4 consolidated risk(s) drive this decision.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: Plausible consequence pathways require an explicit leadership treatment decision.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Approve linked treatments; any temporary acceptance must name an owner, expiry and compensating control.
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Known risk pathways remain untreated without a documented acceptance basis.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: Signed treatment decision for every Critical and High risk.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Approve the target control standards management will implement across the priority risk areas.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: 15 linked finding(s) and 15 consolidated risk(s) drive this decision.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: Functions need one design baseline rather than independent interpretations of the findings.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Adopt the control-improvement register; deviations require documented oversight approval.
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Partial or inconsistent designs fail to address the causal pathway.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: Approved design baseline and named implementation owners.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Approve specialist capacity and resources for high-difficulty controls.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: 6 linked finding(s) and 6 consolidated risk(s) drive this decision.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: High-difficulty controls cannot meet target periods without committed capacity.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Fund the named supporting functions and require a resource-confirmed delivery plan.
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: The highest-complexity gaps remain open despite nominal approval.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: Resource plan showing accountable people, capacity and approved spend.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Approve prerequisite-first sequencing for dependent improvements.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: 15 linked finding(s) and 15 consolidated risk(s) drive this decision.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: Dependent controls cannot operate reliably before prerequisite ownership, data or processes exist.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Use authoritative roadmap dependency IDs and escalate threatened prerequisites.
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Downstream controls are implemented on incomplete foundations.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: Dependency-confirmed delivery sequence with escalation owners.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Approve a fixed fraud-risk implementation and control-effectiveness review cadence.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: 3 linked finding(s) and 3 consolidated risk(s) drive this decision.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: The linked registers require continuing governance to become a managed programme.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Require monthly implementation reporting and quarterly control-effectiveness review through the organisation’s management and oversight route.
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Actions lose momentum, exceptions remain open and management receives the control position too late to intervene.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: First governance-pack date, owner, control-effectiveness measures and overdue escalation fields.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "Priority feed outage, high-risk alert outside SLA or confirmed compromise not escalated." and deliver the exact control design: The security monitoring owner inventories material login, privilege, profile and transaction events, implements risk rules across the full in-scope event feed, assigns alerts to trained analysts, preserves dispositions and escalates high-risk account compromise immediately; monthly tuning uses confirmed true/false positives.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Information Security / Risk
roadmapActions.successMeasure: All priority event feeds monitored and 95% of high-risk alerts triaged within SLA.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Alert case records; In-scope event inventory; Monitoring-rule catalogue; Monthly tuning and coverage report
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Priority feed outage, high-risk alert outside SLA or confirmed compromise not escalated.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "Any missed quarterly review, unassigned account or removal overdue beyond 10 business days." and deliver the exact control design: System owners must maintain a current role-to-access matrix, require business-owner approval against the requester’s current duties before granting access, separate incompatible initiation and approval rights, and retain the request, approval and provisioning trail.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Risk / Internal Audit
roadmapActions.successMeasure: 100% population reviewed quarterly and 95% of removal exceptions closed within 10 business days.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Access requests and approvals; Current role-to-access matrix; Provisioning audit trail; Segregation-of-duties exception decisions
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any missed quarterly review, unassigned account or removal overdue beyond 10 business days.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "A suspected takeover that cannot be reconstructed from logs, or a material system without identity logging." and deliver the exact control design: Security Operations must monitor authentication, credential, profile, device and transaction signals across material identity-bearing systems, define takeover indicators and alert thresholds, and route suspected identity misuse into the separate investigation and containment process.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Information Security / Risk
roadmapActions.successMeasure: All material identity-bearing systems are logged with takeover alerting active and the runbook exercised annually.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Alert definitions for takeover indicators; Defined retention period and data-protection basis; Investigation runbook and a worked case example; Log coverage inventory for identity-bearing systems
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: A suspected takeover that cannot be reconstructed from logs, or a material system without identity logging.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "Activation before verification, an unapproved exception, or a sensitive change without re-verification." and deliver the exact control design: The process owner must define the risk points requiring verification, including customer or beneficiary enrolment, employee onboarding, supplier activation and counterparty contracting. Apply proportionate checks against independent sources such as identity documents validated for authenticity, company registration records and confirmation of contact details through independently obtained channels. Retain results and evidence under applicable data-protection obligations, require documented approval for exceptions, and trigger re-verification for sensitive profile or banking changes.
roadmapActions.processOwner: Process owners for onboarding and activation
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Risk / Compliance
roadmapActions.successMeasure: 100% of in-scope enrolments and activations carry completed verification before activation, with all exceptions approved.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Defined verification risk points and required checks; Exception approvals; re-verification records for sensitive changes; Verification records with source and date
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Activation before verification, an unapproved exception, or a sensitive change without re-verification.
roadmapActions.accountableOwner: Process owners for onboarding and activation

roadmapActions.domainName: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "Review overdue, or a concentration of exceptions by one individual not investigated." and deliver the exact control design: The audit committee must commission periodic independent review of procurement and vendor management covering all vendor-master creations and amendments with approver identity, award patterns by buyer and supplier, spend outside approved contracts or thresholds, use of emergency and single-source routes, and policy exception volumes by individual; findings are reported to governance with owners and due dates and tracked to closure.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Audit Committee
roadmapActions.successMeasure: An independent procurement and vendor-management review is completed each period with findings closed by due date.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Award and exception pattern analysis by individual; Findings tracked to closure; Independent review scope and report; Vendor-master change log with approvers
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Review overdue, or a concentration of exceptions by one individual not investigated.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "A suspected compromise report unactioned beyond target, or no route published for a live user-facing channel." and deliver the exact control design: The security operations owner must publish a clearly signposted route for staff and, where relevant, external users to report suspicious messages, unexpected account changes and suspected compromise, define monitored hours and target response times, connect reports directly into the alert triage and incident-response process, provide acknowledgement and outcome feedback, and track reporting volume and response time against target.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Information Security / Risk
roadmapActions.successMeasure: At least 95% of reports acknowledged within the target time and routed into triage.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Defined response-time targets; Evidence reports feed into triage and incident response; Published reporting routes for staff and users; Report register with response times
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: A suspected compromise report unactioned beyond target, or no route published for a live user-facing channel.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "A sensitive payroll change released without review, unexplained duplicate or ghost record, or unresolved exception at payment release." and deliver the exact control design: Payroll and Human Resources must reconcile joiner, mover and leaver records to the payroll master file before each payment run, independently review bank-account and pay-rate changes, test for duplicate or ghost records and unusual payments, and retain reviewer decisions and exception closure before release.
roadmapActions.accountableExecutive: Chief Financial Officer / Chief People Officer
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Finance Control / Internal Audit
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Every payroll run has a completed independent pre-payment review with all exceptions resolved or formally escalated.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Duplicate and ghost-record exception report; Exception closure evidence; Joiner/mover/leaver reconciliation; Payroll master-file change report; Pre-payroll review sign-off
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: A sensitive payroll change released without review, unexplained duplicate or ghost record, or unresolved exception at payment release.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "Unexplained shortage or overage above threshold, missing count or unreconciled banking." and deliver the exact control design: Finance and site managers must assign cash custodians, perform opening and closing counts with independent review, reconcile takings to receipts and bankings, record sealed transfers and investigate every shortage or overage against a defined threshold before the next cycle closes.
roadmapActions.accountableExecutive: Chief Financial Officer / Chief Operating Officer
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Finance Control / Internal Audit
roadmapActions.successMeasure: All cash points reconcile each cycle, with every difference investigated and resolved or escalated within the defined period.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Banking and receipt reconciliation; Cash custody register; Count sheets and independent checks; Sealed transfer records; Shortage/overage investigation log
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Unexplained shortage or overage above threshold, missing count or unreconciled banking.

roadmapActions.domainName: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "Criteria set or changed after bid opening, an undeclared conflict, or unjustified single-source award." and deliver the exact control design: The procurement owner must require, above defined thresholds, that evaluation criteria and weightings are fixed and recorded before submissions are opened, submissions remain sealed until a scheduled opening witnessed by at least two people, evaluation is performed by a panel with signed conflict declarations, and single-source or emergency awards require documented justification and independent approval; a periodic analysis reviews award concentration, repeated near-identical pricing and rotating winners.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Internal Audit / Risk
roadmapActions.successMeasure: 100% of above-threshold awards follow the documented competitive process with declared conflicts and justified exceptions.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Award concentration and pricing-pattern analysis; Panel conflict declarations and scoring sheets; Pre-set evaluation criteria dated before submission opening; Sealed-bid opening records with witnesses; Single-source justifications and approvals
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Criteria set or changed after bid opening, an undeclared conflict, or unjustified single-source award.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "Unknown or unjustified access, missed review, or removal overdue beyond the agreed service level." and deliver the exact control design: IT Security must reconcile the complete sensitive-access and administrator population to current owners and role requirements at least quarterly, obtain an independent keep/remove decision from system owners, record exceptions and close removals within the defined service level; emergency and service accounts are included.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Information Security / Internal Audit
roadmapActions.successMeasure: 100% of sensitive and administrator access is reviewed each quarter, with removals completed within the defined service level.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Complete sensitive-access register; Quarterly recertification decisions; Removal and exception tickets; Role and business-justification evidence
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Unknown or unjustified access, missed review, or removal overdue beyond the agreed service level.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "Missed review, unknown access or removal overdue beyond the defined service level." and deliver the exact control design: System owners must export the complete active-user access population on a defined cycle, obtain business-owner keep/remove decisions against current responsibilities, route exceptions to IT for closure and reconcile leaver and mover removals to the HR feed.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Risk / Internal Audit
roadmapActions.successMeasure: 100% of ordinary system and data access is reviewed on schedule and stale access is removed within the defined service level.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Complete user-access export; Current role-to-access matrix; Periodic review decisions; Removal and exception tickets
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Missed review, unknown access or removal overdue beyond the defined service level.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "Material unexplained shrinkage, unsupported disposal or missed count at a high-risk location." and deliver the exact control design: Operations and Finance must maintain a complete stock and asset register, assign custodians, require authorised movement and disposal records, perform risk-based counts across locations, reconcile results to the ledger or inventory system and independently approve write-offs and investigate shrinkage exceptions.
roadmapActions.accountableExecutive: Chief Operating Officer / Chief Financial Officer
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Finance Control / Internal Audit
roadmapActions.successMeasure: All material stock and physical assets are counted and reconciled on schedule, with shrinkage and write-offs independently reviewed.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Complete stock and asset register; Count sheets and reconciliation; Custodian assignments; Movement and disposal records; Write-off and shrinkage review
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Material unexplained shrinkage, unsupported disposal or missed count at a high-risk location.

roadmapActions.domainName: Third-Party and Supply Chain Fraud Risk
roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "A high-risk third party overdue for review, or an ownership change detected without reassessment." and deliver the exact control design: The vendor-risk owner must define a risk-based monitoring cycle in which high-risk third parties are re-screened for ownership and sanctions change, reviewed for delivery and quality performance, tested for pricing drift against benchmark or contract, and analysed for spend concentration and unusual growth; findings requiring action are logged with owners, and failure to complete a cycle triggers escalation to the CFO.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Risk / Internal Audit
roadmapActions.successMeasure: 100% of high-risk third parties reviewed within the defined cycle with findings actioned by due date.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Action log with owners; Performance and pricing review records; Re-screening results for ownership and sanctions; Risk-tiered monitoring schedule; Spend concentration analysis
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: A high-risk third party overdue for review, or an ownership change detected without reassessment.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "A high-risk role group with low report rate, or a real payment instruction actioned without out-of-band verification." and deliver the exact control design: The security awareness owner must deliver role-relevant training covering payment-instruction and bank-detail-change requests, executive impersonation, urgency and secrecy pressure, credential-harvesting pages and voice or messaging impersonation; reinforce with periodic simulations targeted at high-risk roles such as finance and procurement, measure report rate as well as click rate, provide a one-click reporting route with feedback, and require verification through an independently obtained channel for any payment or bank-detail instruction.
roadmapActions.accountableExecutive: Chief Technology Officer / Chief People Officer
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Information Security / Risk
roadmapActions.successMeasure: At least 95% completion, improving report rate and declining click rate across successive simulations.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Reporting route usage statistics; Role-relevant training content and completion records; Simulation results including click and report rates; Verification procedure for payment and bank-detail instructions
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: A high-risk role group with low report rate, or a real payment instruction actioned without out-of-band verification.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Apply immediate escalation at "Suspected takeover not contained within the defined SLA, incomplete evidence or unresolved affected-party exposure." and deliver the exact control design: Security Operations and Fraud Operations must maintain a response runbook for identity misuse covering session revocation, credential reset, account hold, customer or employee contact, evidence preservation, scope assessment, recovery, escalation and closure; the runbook is exercised periodically and material cases receive independent review.
roadmapActions.accountableExecutive: Chief Technology Officer / Chief Operating Officer
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: Information Security / Risk
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Every suspected identity-misuse case has timely containment, a recorded investigation and an accountable closure decision.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Authentication and activity evidence; Containment and investigation case records; Exercise and lessons-learned records; Identity-misuse response runbook; Recovery or notification decisions
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Suspected takeover not contained within the defined SLA, incomplete evidence or unresolved affected-party exposure.

essentialModel.conclusion: Fictional Retail Group (extensive unanswered information) is not starting from zero. Its fraud leadership and governance and continuous improvement and fraud risk monitoring provide a useful foundation. The weakness is that these capabilities are not yet connected into a repeatable fraud-risk cycle, so ownership, challenge, detection and response do not yet reinforce one another. The next 90-day checkpoint should test whether ownership now operate as one system rather than as separate activities.
essentialModel.reportBasis: This report is based on management's responses to the MK Fraud Readiness assessment and MK's analytical methodology. It provides fraud-risk analysis and control-design guidance. MK has not independently tested whether controls operate in practice.

decisionAgenda.decisionRequired: Approve accountable executive mandates and escalation authority for priority remediation.
decisionAgenda.whyNow: Hard-gate, governance and maturity-limiting controls require authority to allocate resources and resolve blockers.
decisionAgenda.recommendedDirection: Name one accountable executive per linked control and approve a 30-day escalation route.
decisionAgenda.consequenceOfDelay: Priority controls remain ownerless or blocked and the maturity reading remains constrained.

decisionAgenda.decisionRequired: Choose and record remediation rather than passive acceptance for Critical and High risks.
decisionAgenda.whyNow: Plausible consequence pathways require an explicit leadership treatment decision.
decisionAgenda.recommendedDirection: Approve linked treatments; any temporary acceptance must name an owner, expiry and compensating control.
decisionAgenda.consequenceOfDelay: Known risk pathways remain untreated without a documented acceptance basis.

decisionAgenda.decisionRequired: Approve the target control standards management will implement across the priority risk areas.
decisionAgenda.whyNow: Functions need one design baseline rather than independent interpretations of the findings.
decisionAgenda.recommendedDirection: Adopt the control-improvement register; deviations require documented oversight approval.
decisionAgenda.consequenceOfDelay: Partial or inconsistent designs fail to address the causal pathway.

decisionAgenda.decisionRequired: Approve specialist capacity and resources for high-difficulty controls.
decisionAgenda.whyNow: High-difficulty controls cannot meet target periods without committed capacity.
decisionAgenda.recommendedDirection: Fund the named supporting functions and require a resource-confirmed delivery plan.
decisionAgenda.consequenceOfDelay: The highest-complexity gaps remain open despite nominal approval.

decisionAgenda.decisionRequired: Approve prerequisite-first sequencing for dependent improvements.
decisionAgenda.whyNow: Dependent controls cannot operate reliably before prerequisite ownership, data or processes exist.
decisionAgenda.recommendedDirection: Use authoritative roadmap dependency IDs and escalate threatened prerequisites.
decisionAgenda.consequenceOfDelay: Downstream controls are implemented on incomplete foundations.

decisionAgenda.decisionRequired: Approve a fixed fraud-risk implementation and control-effectiveness review cadence.
decisionAgenda.whyNow: The linked registers require continuing governance to become a managed programme.
decisionAgenda.recommendedDirection: Require monthly implementation reporting and quarterly control-effectiveness review through the organisation’s management and oversight route.
decisionAgenda.consequenceOfDelay: Actions lose momentum, exceptions remain open and management receives the control position too late to intervene.

controls.targetState: Risk-based monitoring covers material digital events, alerts are triaged to defined SLAs and rules are tuned from confirmed outcomes.
controls.controlDesign: The security monitoring owner inventories material login, privilege, profile and transaction events, implements risk rules across the full in-scope event feed, assigns alerts to trained analysts, preserves dispositions and escalates high-risk account compromise immediately; monthly tuning uses confirmed true/false positives.
controls.oversightFunction: Information Security / Risk
controls.operatingFrequency: Continuous monitoring; monthly rule tuning
controls.populationCoverage: The complete in-scope population for continuous monitoring; monthly rule tuning must be reconciled before sampling.
controls.effectivenessTest: All priority event feeds monitored and 95% of high-risk alerts triaged within SLA.
controls.escalationThreshold: Priority feed outage, high-risk alert outside SLA or confirmed compromise not escalated.

controls.currentState: Initial / ad hoc: Exists only informally or inconsistently.; self-assessed and not independently verified.
controls.controlObjective: Close the material control weakness recorded for "Employees receive training on phishing, social engineering and digital impersonation attempts".
controls.targetState: Training is role-relevant, reinforced by periodic simulations, measured by behaviour rather than completion alone, and supported by a fast reporting route with feedback.
controls.controlDesign: The security awareness owner must deliver role-relevant training covering payment-instruction and bank-detail-change requests, executive impersonation, urgency and secrecy pressure, credential-harvesting pages and voice or messaging impersonation; reinforce with periodic simulations targeted at high-risk roles such as finance and procurement, measure report rate as well as click rate, provide a one-click reporting route with feedback, and require verification through an independently obtained channel for any payment or bank-detail instruction.
controls.accountableExecutiveRole: Chief Technology Officer / Chief People Officer
controls.oversightFunction: Information Security / Risk
controls.operatingFrequency: At induction, at least annually, with periodic simulations
controls.populationCoverage: The complete in-scope population for at induction, at least annually, with periodic simulations must be reconciled before sampling.
dependencies: Payment verification controls; Reporting route for suspicious messages
controls.effectivenessTest: At least 95% completion, improving report rate and declining click rate across successive simulations.
controls.escalationThreshold: A high-risk role group with low report rate, or a real payment instruction actioned without out-of-band verification.

controls.currentState: Not in place: No control exists.; self-assessed and not independently verified.
controls.controlObjective: Close the material control weakness recorded for "Employees and users know how to report suspicious digital activity or account-security concerns".
controls.targetState: Reporting routes are published for both staff and external users, monitored during defined hours with defined response times, and feed directly into monitoring and incident response.
controls.controlDesign: The security operations owner must publish a clearly signposted route for staff and, where relevant, external users to report suspicious messages, unexpected account changes and suspected compromise, define monitored hours and target response times, connect reports directly into the alert triage and incident-response process, provide acknowledgement and outcome feedback, and track reporting volume and response time against target.
controls.oversightFunction: Information Security / Risk
controls.operatingFrequency: Continuous intake within defined monitored hours
controls.populationCoverage: The complete in-scope population for continuous intake within defined monitored hours must be reconciled before sampling.
dependencies: Incident response plan; Monitoring and triage process
controls.effectivenessTest: At least 95% of reports acknowledged within the target time and routed into triage.
controls.escalationThreshold: A suspected compromise report unactioned beyond target, or no route published for a live user-facing channel.

controls.currentState: Initial / ad hoc: Exists only informally or inconsistently.; self-assessed and not independently verified.
controls.controlObjective: Close the material control weakness recorded for "The organisation can detect identity misuse, account takeover or impersonation".
controls.targetState: Material identity-bearing systems and digital channels produce sufficient authentication, profile and activity signals to identify suspected identity misuse promptly.
controls.controlDesign: Security Operations must monitor authentication, credential, profile, device and transaction signals across material identity-bearing systems, define takeover indicators and alert thresholds, and route suspected identity misuse into the separate investigation and containment process.
controls.oversightFunction: Information Security / Risk
controls.operatingFrequency: Continuous logging and alerting; runbook exercised at least annually
controls.populationCoverage: The complete in-scope population for continuous logging and alerting; runbook exercised at least annually must be reconciled before sampling.
controls.effectivenessTest: All material identity-bearing systems are logged with takeover alerting active and the runbook exercised annually.
controls.escalationThreshold: A suspected takeover that cannot be reconstructed from logs, or a material system without identity logging.

controls.currentState: Initial / ad hoc: Exists only informally or inconsistently.; self-assessed and not independently verified.
controls.controlObjective: Close the material control weakness recorded for "Sensitive access and administrator rights are reviewed periodically".
controls.targetState: The complete sensitive-access and administrator population is independently recertified on a defined cycle, with stale, excessive or unjustified rights removed and exceptions escalated.
controls.controlDesign: IT Security must reconcile the complete sensitive-access and administrator population to current owners and role requirements at least quarterly, obtain an independent keep/remove decision from system owners, record exceptions and close removals within the defined service level; emergency and service accounts are included.
controls.oversightFunction: Information Security / Internal Audit
controls.operatingFrequency: Quarterly and after material role or system change
controls.populationCoverage: The complete in-scope population for quarterly and after material role or system change must be reconciled before sampling.
dependencies: Authoritative identity inventory; HR joiner/mover/leaver feed
controls.effectivenessTest: 100% of sensitive and administrator access is reviewed each quarter, with removals completed within the defined service level.
controls.escalationThreshold: Unknown or unjustified access, missed review, or removal overdue beyond the agreed service level.

controls.currentState: Partially designed: Partially designed but not fully implemented.; self-assessed and not independently verified.
controls.controlObjective: Close the material control weakness recorded for "The organisation can investigate and contain identity misuse, account takeover or impersonation".
controls.targetState: Suspected identity misuse has a named response owner, defined containment actions, investigation steps, evidence requirements and closure or recovery decisions.
controls.controlDesign: Security Operations and Fraud Operations must maintain a response runbook for identity misuse covering session revocation, credential reset, account hold, customer or employee contact, evidence preservation, scope assessment, recovery, escalation and closure; the runbook is exercised periodically and material cases receive independent review.
controls.accountableExecutiveRole: Chief Technology Officer / Chief Operating Officer
controls.oversightFunction: Information Security / Risk
controls.operatingFrequency: On every suspected case; annual or post-incident exercise
controls.populationCoverage: The complete in-scope population for on every suspected case; annual or post-incident exercise must be reconciled before sampling.
dependencies: Identity and activity logging; Incident-response process
controls.effectivenessTest: Every suspected identity-misuse case has timely containment, a recorded investigation and an accountable closure decision.
controls.escalationThreshold: Suspected takeover not contained within the defined SLA, incomplete evidence or unresolved affected-party exposure.

scenarios.title: A compromised or impersonated identity is used to change a sensitive profile, instruction or transaction
scenarios.actorClass: An internal or external actor using an impersonated or insufficiently verified identity
scenarios.opportunity: Identity verification at material risk points is not yet applied consistently enough to prevent misuse.
scenarios.entryPoint: A customer account, payment instruction or profile is created or materially changed through a digital channel without an independent verification step.
scenarios.mechanism: An actor uses an impersonated or insufficiently verified identity to obtain payment, credit or account authority through the organisation's digital channel.
scenarios.concealment: The activity may appear routine until complete population review, independent approval or exception monitoring exposes it.
scenarios.consequence: Unauthorised access, payment, benefit or profile change can occur before the identity or transaction is challenged. compromised or privileged access can alter records and transactions. Digital misuse can evade prevention and monitoring.
warningIndicators: Activation before verification, an unapproved exception, or a sensitive change without re-verification.
An exception, access, approval or incident record that cannot be reconciled to the complete in-scope population.
Credential reset, device change or profile amendment
Identity data differs across trusted records
Sensitive transaction follows a new or unusual session
scenarios.controlWeakness: Identity verification and sensitive-change monitoring are partially designed.
scenarios.interruptionPoint: Security Operations must monitor authentication, credential, profile, device and transaction signals across material identity-bearing systems, define takeover indicators and alert thresholds, and route suspected identity misuse into the separate investigation and containment process.; The process owner must define the risk points requiring verification, including customer or beneficiary enrolment, employee onboarding, supplier activation and counterparty contracting. Apply proportionate checks against independent sources such as identity documents validated for authenticity, company registration records and confirmation of contact details through independently obtained channels. Retain results and evidence under applicable data-protection obligations, require documented approval for exceptions, and trigger re-verification for sensitive profile or banking changes.
scenarios.immediateContainment: Pause the sensitive change or transaction, re-perform identity verification through a trusted route and preserve authentication records.
scenarios.longTermResponse: Implement risk-based identity verification, profile-change controls, authentication evidence and takeover investigation.

scenarios.title: Unusual activity avoids timely challenge because monitoring or escalation coverage is incomplete
scenarios.actorClass: An internal or external actor using an unusual transaction pattern
scenarios.opportunity: Monitoring and exception review are not yet sufficiently deliberate or repeatable to challenge unusual activity promptly.
scenarios.entryPoint: A refund, credit note or manual adjustment falls outside the expected pattern without a timely review route.
scenarios.mechanism: An actor keeps refunds, credits or adjustments individually small and routine so they remain below or outside the available monitoring and exception thresholds.
scenarios.concealment: The activity may appear routine until complete population review, independent approval or exception monitoring exposes it.
scenarios.consequence: Delayed detection allows suspicious activity or losses to continue and exceptions to accumulate. compromised or privileged access can alter records and transactions. Digital misuse can evade prevention and monitoring.
warningIndicators: An exception, access, approval or incident record that cannot be reconciled to the complete in-scope population.
Priority feed outage, high-risk alert outside SLA or confirmed compromise not escalated.
Repeated low-value or threshold-adjacent activity
Alert or exception backlog grows without assigned owner
Monitoring rule is not updated after a material process change
scenarios.controlWeakness: Monitoring and exception review are at an initial or ad hoc stage.
scenarios.interruptionPoint: The security monitoring owner inventories material login, privilege, profile and transaction events, implements risk rules across the full in-scope event feed, assigns alerts to trained analysts, preserves dispositions and escalates high-risk account compromise immediately; monthly tuning uses confirmed true/false positives.
scenarios.immediateContainment: Assign and triage the affected alerts or exceptions, preserve the relevant activity record and escalate overdue items.
scenarios.longTermResponse: Define monitoring coverage, red flags, review ownership, closure evidence and threshold-change governance.

scenarios.title: Third-party relationship manipulation or collusion escapes timely challenge
scenarios.actorClass: A third party acting for or with the organisation, alone or with an insider able to influence the relationship
scenarios.opportunity: A weakness in how a third-party relationship is assessed, governed or reviewed can leave manipulation or collusion insufficiently challenged.
scenarios.entryPoint: A third-party relationship continues, or changes, without the review the organisation intends to apply to it.
scenarios.mechanism: An actor uses the gap left by that weakness to obtain value or advantage through the relationship while it continues to appear routine.
scenarios.concealment: An actor relies on ordinary-looking activity, weak exception review or incomplete audit records to avoid timely challenge.
scenarios.consequence: Value or advantage can move through a third-party relationship before the arrangement is independently challenged.
warningIndicators: A procurement or vendor-master review is overdue
Exceptions concentrate with one individual without investigation
A third-party relationship or the decision affecting it proceeds without independent challenge
scenarios.controlWeakness: "Procurement or vendor-management activity is subject to oversight or periodic review" is recorded as "Not in place".
scenarios.interruptionPoint: The Governing body / independent oversight must commission periodic independent review of procurement and vendor management covering all vendor-master creations and amendments with approver identity, award patterns by buyer and supplier, spend outside approved contracts or thresholds, use of emergency and single-source routes, and policy exception volumes by individual; findings are reported to governance with owners and due dates and tracked to closure.
scenarios.immediateContainment: Pause the affected third-party activity where proportionate, preserve the relevant relationship and decision records, and complete the review required by the linked control before further commitment.
scenarios.longTermResponse: Apply the assessment, governance and review disciplines identified by the linked findings consistently across the third-party population, with defined ownership, evidence and escalation.

materialFindings.diagnosis: 5 of the 5 controls answered for this scheme were reported as gaps. Invoices are paid without being checked against what was approved or received. Quantities checked: not in place. Services confirmed: not in place. Most purchases are approved before commitment, through a purchase order or another record. materialFindings.likelyOperationalImpact: Supplier relationships, payment runs and the supplier master file would need to be investigated and corrected.

Goods received notes, the receiving system, a sample matched to payments.

Quantities checked: the answer to "Are delivered quantities checked against the delivery note and the order?" is yes, across everything it should cover. Services confirmed: the answer to "For services, does the person receiving the service confirm it was delivered before payment?" is yes, across everything it should cover. controlImprovements.controlObjective: Stop the scheme where invoices are paid for goods or services not received or not agreed.

Quantities checked: the answer to "Are delivered quantities checked against the delivery note and the order?" is yes, across everything it should cover. 3. Services confirmed: the answer to "For services, does the person receiving the service confirm it was delivered before payment?" is yes, across everything it should cover. 4. Approved order before commitment: Every purchase is approved by someone with the authority to do so before the organisation commits, and the approval is recorded. 5. Receipt recorded before payment: Receipt is always recorded before the related invoice is paid.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Name one accountable executive for each area with first-priority schemes open or unsupported: procurement and third parties (6), people and payroll (5), digital and identity (5), customers and revenue (4) and cash, stock and assets (2).
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: 22 first-priority schemes have a control that stops them reported as a gap, and 0 rely on a control whose own practices were reported as gaps.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: Each scheme needs one person with authority over the process, the system and the people involved.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Head of procurement or CFO for procurement and third parties, HR or payroll manager for people and payroll, Head of IT or IT provider for digital and identity and Commercial or finance manager for customers and revenue.
leadershipDecisions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Schemes with no owner stay open, and the gaps that let them happen stay unassigned.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: A signed list of schemes, their accountable executives and target dates.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Approve the target design for procurement and third parties, where 6 first-priority schemes are open or unsupported.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: A fictitious supplier is created and paid; Supplier payments are diverted through changed bank details; A supplier is set up with an account it does not own
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: The schemes share processes and owners; designing them together avoids separate partial fixes.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Every new supplier goes through a defined process, with set checks and an approval, before it can be paid. Directors compared with staff: the answer to "Do you compare supplier directors, owners, addresses or bank accounts with your employee records?" is yes, across everything it should cover. Dormant suppliers deactivated: the answer to "Are suppliers that have not been used for a set period deactivated?" is yes, across everything it should cover. Suppliers re-checked: the answer to "Are existing suppliers re-checked periodically, not only when they are first added?" is yes, across everything it should cover. Directors and owners, including those behind holding companies, are identified for every new supplier from an independent source.
leadershipDecisions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Controls are added one at a time and the scheme stays open through the gaps between them.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: An approved control design with owners, operating cycle and the records each step leaves.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Put first the controls that other controls depend on.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: Directors compared with staff is not in place, so how the staff comparison is done cannot operate; Dormant suppliers deactivated is not in place, so reactivation approved cannot operate; Services confirmed is not in place, so confirmation tied to deliverables cannot operate.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: Building the dependent checks first produces controls that cannot run.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Sequence directors compared with staff, dormant suppliers deactivated, services confirmed and three-way match ahead of the checks that rely on them.
leadershipDecisions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Effort is spent on checks that cannot operate.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Decide whether to keep relying on 1 control reported in place whose supporting practices were reported as gaps.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: Code accessible to staff: 1 supporting practice reported as gaps.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: A self-reported control that its own practices do not support can give management comfort it has not earned.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Ask each process owner to confirm in writing how the control works without the missing practices, and close the practices in the next 60 days.
leadershipDecisions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: The scheme is treated as covered when it may not be.
leadershipDecisions.immediateNextDeliverable: Written confirmation from each process owner.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Require the 7 outstanding answers within 30 days, and treat any that cannot be given as an open risk.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: Nothing is concluded about a control nobody has answered for; until it is answered the scheme it stops is unknown, not covered.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: Assign each outstanding answer to a named person with a date.
leadershipDecisions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Schemes stay unknown and cannot be prioritised.

leadershipDecisions.decisionRequired: Have the board or its audit committee receive the status of the 22 first-priority schemes each month until they are closed.
leadershipDecisions.evidenceDrivingIt: 22 first-priority schemes open or unsupported across 5 areas.
leadershipDecisions.whyNow: Monthly reporting keeps the schemes visible to the people who can remove blockers.
leadershipDecisions.recommendedDecision: A one-page scheme status: owner, controls in place, controls outstanding, next date.
leadershipDecisions.implementationOwner: Risk manager or fraud risk lead
leadershipDecisions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
leadershipDecisions.consequenceOfDelay: Progress is not visible until the next assessment.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Obtain the 7 outstanding answers (2 on controls that stop a scheme) from Risk and investigations, HR and payroll, Finance and Operations and sales and 1 other functions, and record any that cannot be answered as an open risk.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any outstanding answer on a first-priority scheme still open after 30 days.
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Every outstanding answer is given or recorded as an open risk with a named owner.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: The completed function packages.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Confirm with HR lead or ethics officer how code accessible to staff operates and put in place training on joining.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where staff do not know or understand what is expected, or any case processed without this control: training on joining.
roadmapActions.dependency: Part of a requirement that spans several areas: weaknesses behind a loss are fixed
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show that every case in the period passes this test: Do all employees receive fraud and ethics training when they join?
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: HR lead or ethics officer confirms in writing that the controls operate for every case.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where donations or sponsorships channel bribes: put in place recipients checked for links.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where donations or sponsorships channel bribes, or any case processed without this control: recipients checked for links.
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show that every case in the period passes this test: Are recipients checked for links to public officials, customers' decision-makers and employees before money is committed?
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: CSI or sustainability lead confirms in writing that the controls operate for every case.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where a fictitious supplier is created and paid: put in place new supplier process, directors compared with staff, dormant suppliers deactivated and suppliers re-checked.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where supplier payments are diverted through changed bank details: put in place familiar caller still verified and change confirmed with supplier.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where supplier payments are diverted through changed bank details, or any case processed without this control: familiar caller still verified.
roadmapActions.dependency: Part of a requirement that spans several areas: changes to payment details are verified through a route the requester does not control
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show, for every case in the period: the procedure requires a call back on the number on file regardless of any incoming call or video, and staff know why.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where a supplier is set up with an account it does not own: put in place bank account verified.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where a supplier is set up with an account it does not own, or any case processed without this control: bank account verified.
roadmapActions.dependency: Part of a requirement that spans several areas: accounts are confirmed as belonging to the payee
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show, for every case in the period: every new supplier's account is verified through a bank or third-party service before the first payment.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Account verification results, for example through a bank's account verification service, and the onboarding checklist.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where one person can order and approve payment: put in place orderer is not payment approver.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where one person can order and approve payment, or any case processed without this control: orderer is not payment approver.
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show, for every case in the period: the duties are always separated, or any exception is approved and recorded.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: The delegation of authority, system access lists, a sample of orders and the related payment approvals.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where invoices are paid for goods or services not received or not agreed: put in place three-way match, quantities checked, services confirmed and approved order before commitment.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where invoices are paid for goods or services not received or not agreed, or any case processed without this control: three-way match.
roadmapActions.dependency: Services confirmed is not in place, so confirmation tied to deliverables cannot operate
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show, for every case in the period: every invoice is checked against an approved order, quote or contract and against confirmation of receipt before payment, and differences are resolved first.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Payment files showing the order, receipt and invoice, exception reports. Purchase orders or approval records dated before the invoice, for a sample of recent purchases. Goods received notes, the receiving system, a sample matched to payments.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where an outsourced provider misuses its access: put in place provider access limited.

roadmapActions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where an outsourced provider misuses its access, or any case processed without this control: provider access limited.

roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: The list of providers with access, access settings, the last access review.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where supplier payments are released without two approvals: put in place two approvers on banking platform.

roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where supplier payments are released without two approvals, or any case processed without this control: two approvers on banking platform.
roadmapActions.dependency: Part of a requirement that spans several areas: money leaves only with two independent approvals, enforced where it leaves
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show, for every case in the period: the banking platform requires two separate people to approve every supplier payment.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Banking platform user and approval settings, a sample of payment approvals.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where a tender is manipulated or purchases are split: put in place evaluation against set criteria and quote and tender thresholds.
roadmapActions.processOwner: Head of procurement or bid committee secretary
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where a tender is manipulated or purchases are split, or any case processed without this control: evaluation against set criteria.

roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Evaluation scoresheets, the request for quotation or tender with its criteria, committee minutes.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where buyers take kickbacks: put in place annual interest declarations.

roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where buyers take kickbacks, or any case processed without this control: annual interest declarations.

roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show, for every case in the period: everyone involved in buying declares interests each year and when circumstances change, and declarations are kept on record.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where purchase cards or petty cash are misused: put in place independent reconciliation.

roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where purchase cards or petty cash are misused, or any case processed without this control: independent reconciliation.

roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show that every case in the period passes this test: Are statements reconciled and reviewed by someone other than the cardholder?

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where intermediaries pay bribes or inflate fees: put in place intermediaries vetted.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where procurement anomalies are never noticed: put in place senior review of supplier payments, data reviewed for unusual patterns, split orders monitored and independent review of procurement.

roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where variations inflate the agreed value, or any case processed without this control: variations approved first.

roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show that every case in the period passes this test: Must changes to agreed work, such as variations, extensions or extra scope, be approved before the work goes ahead, whether or not there is a written contract?
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Procurement or the finance manager confirms in writing that the controls operate for every case.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where salaries are redirected through a fake bank change: put in place bank changes confirmed with employee.

roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where salaries are redirected through a fake bank change, or any case processed without this control: bank changes confirmed with employee.
roadmapActions.dependency: Part of a requirement that spans several areas: accounts are confirmed as belonging to the payee
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show, for every case in the period: every change is confirmed through a channel the organisation starts, such as a call to a number on file or in person, before it takes effect.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where ghost employees are paid: put in place payroll reviewed by another person, headcount verification done and independent review of payroll.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where leavers stay on the payroll: put in place leavers removed before next run.

roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show, for every case in the period: every leaver is confirmed as removed before the next pay run, using the HR leaver list.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Leaver lists reconciled to payroll, the pay run checklist.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where a false identity enters at hiring: put in place identity verified and qualifications verified.

roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where a false identity enters at hiring, or any case processed without this control: identity verified.
roadmapActions.dependency: Part of a requirement that spans several areas: identity is established through routes an impersonator cannot control
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show, for every case in the period: every new employee's identity is verified against Home Affairs records, for example through a verification service, before they start.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Verification service results on employee files, the onboarding checklist. Verification results from institutions or SAQA, the recruitment checklist.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where a stand-in or deepfake candidate is appointed: put in place remote appointee identity confirmed.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where a stand-in or deepfake candidate is appointed, or any case processed without this control: remote appointee identity confirmed.
roadmapActions.dependency: Part of a requirement that spans several areas: identity is established through routes an impersonator cannot control
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show, for every case in the period: every remote appointee is confirmed through an in-person meeting or an identity check designed to resist replayed and injected video before access and pay are set up, and failed checks are reviewed by a person.
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: The remote hiring procedure, identity check results, records of in-person meetings.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where the payroll payment file is altered after approval: put in place payment file protected.

roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where the payroll payment file is altered after approval, or any case processed without this control: payment file protected.
roadmapActions.dependency: Part of a requirement that spans several areas: money leaves only with two independent approvals, enforced where it leaves
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show that every case in the period passes this test: Is the payroll payment file protected so that a change between approval and upload to the bank would be prevented or detected, for example through a secure bank connection or a file check that the preparer cannot regenerate?
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Payroll manager or financial controller confirms in writing that the controls operate for every case.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where cash wages are stolen or paid to ghosts: put in place two people pay out cash.

roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show that every case in the period passes this test: Are cash wages paid out by at least two people together?
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Financial controller confirms in writing that the controls operate for every case.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where hours and overtime are inflated: put in place hours approved by supervisor.

roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where hours and overtime are inflated, or any case processed without this control: hours approved by supervisor.
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show that every case in the period passes this test: Are hours approved by a supervisor before they are paid?
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: HR or payroll manager confirms in writing that the controls operate for every case.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where expenses and advances are abused: put in place claims approved by a manager.
roadmapActions.oversightFunction: The board or its audit committee
roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where expenses and advances are abused, or any case processed without this control: claims approved by a manager.
roadmapActions.dependency: Part of a requirement that spans several areas: documents are verified with their source, not on appearance
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show that every case in the period passes this test: Is each claim approved by a manager other than the claimant?
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Financial controller confirms in writing that the controls operate for every case.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where labour brokers invoice for workers who were not there: put in place broker invoices against attendance.

roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where labour brokers invoice for workers who were not there, or any case processed without this control: broker invoices against attendance.
roadmapActions.dependency: Part of a requirement that spans several areas: accounts are confirmed as belonging to the payee
roadmapActions.successMeasure: Management's own records show that every case in the period passes this test: Are labour broker invoices checked against your own attendance records?
roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: Operations manager confirms in writing that the controls operate for every case.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where an insider in a high-risk role works unchecked: put in place block leave required, concerns raised fairly, support for financial pressure and no conflicting duties when covering.

roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where an insider in a high-risk role works unchecked, or any case processed without this control: block leave required.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where refunds are stolen: put in place refunds approved independently, returns received before credit, claim evidence checked for AI and refund patterns reviewed.

roadmapActions.evidenceOfCompletion: A sample of refunds and credit notes with approvals, system workflow settings.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where customer details are changed to divert money or goods: put in place customer detail changes verified, defined onboarding, shared details flagged and business customers verified.

roadmapActions.escalationThreshold: Any suspected case of the scheme where customer details are changed to divert money or goods, or any case processed without this control: customer detail changes verified.

roadmapActions.deliverable: Close the scheme where credit is obtained with fabricated documents: put in place application documents verified, statements sent from the system, limit and terms changes approved and credit approved independently.

cover.centralJudgement: 22 of the organisation's 43 first-priority fraud schemes remain open, most of them in procurement and third parties and people and payroll, and 1 control reported in place is not supported in practice.

diagnosis.title: What is driving the position

rows.pattern: Third parties and supply chain: 6 first-priority schemes open
rows.whyItMatters: Fictitious suppliers enter through onboarding that can be skipped. The same area also leaves open: supplier payments are diverted through changed bank details and a supplier is set up with an account it does not own.

rows.pattern: People, payroll and insider risk: 5 first-priority schemes open
rows.whyItMatters: Salary redirection through fake bank change requests is common and fast. The same area also leaves open: ghost employees are paid and leavers stay on the payroll.

rows.pattern: Digital, cyber-enabled and identity fraud: 5 first-priority schemes open

signals.title: Email never enough on its own
Verification for calls, voice notes and video

rows.whyItMatters: Most business email compromise starts with an account that has no multi-factor authentication. The same area also leaves open: a payment instruction received by email is acted on and a cloned voice or video instruction is obeyed.

rows.pattern: Code accessible to staff: reported in place, not supported by its practices
rows.whyItMatters: It is relied on to stop the scheme where staff do not know or understand what is expected. One self-reported answer says it is in place; the answers about the practices it depends on say otherwise.

diagnosis.interpretation: Of 32 controls reported fully in place that the method can cross-check, 5 were cross-checked with one further self-reported answer about a practice they depend on: 4 consistent, 1 missing information. The other 27 were not cross-checked and nothing is concluded about them. These cross-checks compare the organisation's own answers; they are not tests of operation and they change no figure.

rows.exposure: Invoices are paid for goods or services not received or not agreed
rows.whyItMatters: Invoices paid without checking approval and receipt are how overbilling and fictitious deliveries get paid.
rows.potentialConsequence: Funds paid to a diverted, fictitious or overbilling supplier, often unrecoverable once released.
rows.interruptionPoint: Every invoice is checked against an approved order, quote or contract and against confirmation of receipt before payment, and differences are resolved first.
rows.priorityBasis: First-priority scheme; 5 of the 5 controls answered are gaps.

rows.exposure: Supplier payments are diverted through changed bank details
rows.whyItMatters: Changed supplier bank details are the most common route for payment fraud, and cloned voices now defeat call-backs that rely on recognition.
rows.potentialConsequence: Funds paid to a diverted, fictitious or overbilling supplier, often unrecoverable once released.
rows.interruptionPoint: The procedure requires a call back on the number on file regardless of any incoming call or video, and staff know why.
rows.priorityBasis: First-priority scheme; 2 of the 2 controls answered are gaps.

rows.exposure: Salaries are redirected through a fake bank change
rows.whyItMatters: Salary redirection through fake bank change requests is common and fast.
rows.potentialConsequence: Salaries paid to fictitious, departed or overpaid employees, recurring every pay run until found.
rows.interruptionPoint: Every change is confirmed through a channel the organisation starts, such as a call to a number on file or in person, before it takes effect.
rows.priorityBasis: First-priority scheme; 1 of the 1 controls answered is a gap.

rows.exposure: A payment instruction received by email is acted on
rows.whyItMatters: Acting on payment instructions received by email is how business email compromise succeeds.

assessmentBasis.title: Email never enough on its own

rows.potentialConsequence: Payments, credit or goods released to someone impersonating a supplier, customer, employee or executive.
rows.interruptionPoint: Put in place: email never enough on its own.
rows.priorityBasis: First-priority scheme; 1 of the 1 controls answered is a gap.

Here, invoices are paid without being checked against what was approved or received; quantities checked: not in place.

Duplicate or false invoices
Overpricing, overbilling and inflated variations

scenarios.entryPointShort: Supplier payments are diverted through changed bank details
scenarios.controlBreak: A follow-up call from the 'supplier' is accepted as confirmation. Changes are confirmed, but sometimes using contact details taken from the request itself.
scenarios.controlBreakShort: Familiar caller still verified not in place; change confirmed with supplier partly
scenarios.exposureShort: Payment redirection through false bank details or impersonation
scenarios.howItUnfolds: A fraudster, often impersonating the supplier by email, voice or video, has the bank account changed. Changed supplier bank details are the most common route for payment fraud, and cloned voices now defeat call-backs that rely on recognition. Here, a follow-up call from the 'supplier' is accepted as confirmation; changes are confirmed, but sometimes using contact details taken from the request itself.
warningIndicators: Payment redirection through false bank details or impersonation
scenarios.immediateInterruption: Until the design operates, the process owner checks every new case and the recent ones by hand against this standard: the procedure requires a call back on the number on file regardless of any incoming call or video, and staff know why.

scenarios.entryPointShort: A request that appears to come from an employee changes where their salary is paid
scenarios.controlBreak: Bank detail changes are made as requested.
scenarios.controlBreakShort: Bank changes confirmed with employee not in place
scenarios.exposureShort: Salary redirection through changed bank details
scenarios.howItUnfolds: A request that appears to come from an employee changes where their salary is paid. Salary redirection through fake bank change requests is common and fast. Here, bank detail changes are made as requested.
warningIndicators: Salary redirection through changed bank details
Ghost or fictitious employees and payees
Unauthorised pay increases, allowances or deductions
scenarios.immediateInterruption: Until the design operates, the process owner checks every new case and the recent ones by hand against this standard: every change is confirmed through a channel the organisation starts, such as a call to a number on file or in person, before it takes effect.

essentialModel.conclusion: Fictional Retail Group (extensive unanswered information) is not starting from zero: 45 schemes have every control that stops them reported in place. The work is concentrated. 22 first-priority schemes, most of them in procurement and third parties, people and payroll and digital and identity, need the specific controls named in this report, owned by the people the method names for them. Management should also not rely on the control reported in place whose own practices were reported as gaps until its owner confirms how it works.
essentialModel.reportBasis: This report is based on the organisation's own answers to the MK Fraud Readiness review, given by the respondent and the accountable functions named in it, and read against the draft review method, which MK has not yet approved. MK has not independently tested whether controls operate in practice, and no evidence was reviewed; evidence review is a separate Advisory service. decisionAgenda.decisionRequired: Name one accountable executive for each area with first-priority schemes open or unsupported: procurement and third parties (6), people and payroll (5), digital and identity (5), customers and revenue (4) and cash, stock and assets (2).
decisionAgenda.whyNow: Each scheme needs one person with authority over the process, the system and the people involved.
decisionAgenda.recommendedDirection: Head of procurement or CFO for procurement and third parties, HR or payroll manager for people and payroll, Head of IT or IT provider for digital and identity and Commercial or finance manager for customers and revenue.
decisionAgenda.consequenceOfDelay: Schemes with no owner stay open, and the gaps that let them happen stay unassigned.

decisionAgenda.decisionRequired: Approve the target design for procurement and third parties, where 6 first-priority schemes are open or unsupported.
decisionAgenda.whyNow: The schemes share processes and owners; designing them together avoids separate partial fixes.
decisionAgenda.recommendedDirection: Every new supplier goes through a defined process, with set checks and an approval, before it can be paid. Directors compared with staff: the answer to "Do you compare supplier directors, owners, addresses or bank accounts with your employee records?" is yes, across everything it should cover. Dormant suppliers deactivated: the answer to "Are suppliers that have not been used for a set period deactivated?" is yes, across everything it should cover. Suppliers re-checked: the answer to "Are existing suppliers re-checked periodically, not only when they are first added?" is yes, across everything it should cover. Directors and owners, including those behind holding companies, are identified for every new supplier from an independent source.
decisionAgenda.consequenceOfDelay: Controls are added one at a time and the scheme stays open through the gaps between them.

decisionAgenda.decisionRequired: Put first the controls that other controls depend on.
decisionAgenda.whyNow: Building the dependent checks first produces controls that cannot run.
decisionAgenda.recommendedDirection: Sequence directors compared with staff, dormant suppliers deactivated, services confirmed and three-way match ahead of the checks that rely on them.
decisionAgenda.consequenceOfDelay: Effort is spent on checks that cannot operate.

decisionAgenda.decisionRequired: Decide whether to keep relying on 1 control reported in place whose supporting practices were reported as gaps.
decisionAgenda.whyNow: A self-reported control that its own practices do not support can give management comfort it has not earned.
decisionAgenda.recommendedDirection: Ask each process owner to confirm in writing how the control works without the missing practices, and close the practices in the next 60 days.
decisionAgenda.consequenceOfDelay: The scheme is treated as covered when it may not be.

decisionAgenda.decisionRequired: Require the 7 outstanding answers within 30 days, and treat any that cannot be given as an open risk.
decisionAgenda.whyNow: Nothing is concluded about a control nobody has answered for; until it is answered the scheme it stops is unknown, not covered.
decisionAgenda.recommendedDirection: Assign each outstanding answer to a named person with a date.
decisionAgenda.consequenceOfDelay: Schemes stay unknown and cannot be prioritised.

decisionAgenda.decisionRequired: Have the board or its audit committee receive the status of the 22 first-priority schemes each month until they are closed.
decisionAgenda.whyNow: Monthly reporting keeps the schemes visible to the people who can remove blockers.
decisionAgenda.recommendedDirection: A one-page scheme status: owner, controls in place, controls outstanding, next date.
decisionAgenda.consequenceOfDelay: Progress is not visible until the next assessment.

findings.assessedPosition: Invoices are paid without being checked against what was approved or received.
findings.assessedDiagnosis: 5 of the 5 controls answered for this scheme were reported as gaps. Invoices are paid without being checked against what was approved or received. Quantities checked: not in place. Services confirmed: not in place. Most purchases are approved before commitment, through a purchase order or another record. Receipt is recorded for most deliveries, but not always before payment. Reported by Procurement, Operations and sales and Finance; not independently tested.
findings.fraudMechanism: Overbilling, fictitious deliveries or inflated rates are paid. The method links it to unauthorised commitments and approval override, duplicate or false invoices, overpricing, overbilling and inflated variations, goods or services paid for but not received, counterfeit, substituted or substandard goods and misrepresented supplier credentials.
findings.whyItMatters: Invoices paid without checking approval and receipt are how overbilling and fictitious deliveries get paid.

findings.assessedPosition: A follow-up call from the 'supplier' is accepted as confirmation.
findings.assessedDiagnosis: 2 of the 2 controls answered for this scheme were reported as gaps. A follow-up call from the 'supplier' is accepted as confirmation. Changes are confirmed, but sometimes using contact details taken from the request itself. Reported by the respondent; not independently tested.
findings.fraudMechanism: A fraudster, often impersonating the supplier by email, voice or video, has the bank account changed. The method links it to payment redirection through false bank details or impersonation.
findings.whyItMatters: Changed supplier bank details are the most common route for payment fraud, and cloned voices now defeat call-backs that rely on recognition.

findings.assessedPosition: Bank detail changes are made as requested.

findings.fraudMechanism: A request that appears to come from an employee changes where their salary is paid. The method links it to salary redirection through changed bank details, ghost or fictitious employees and payees and unauthorised pay increases, allowances or deductions.
findings.whyItMatters: Salary redirection through fake bank change requests is common and fast.

scenarios.title: Invoices are paid for goods or services not received or not agreed
scenarios.actorClass: An insider, supplier or outsider who finds the step unguarded
scenarios.opportunity: Invoices are paid without being checked against what was approved or received. Quantities checked: not in place. Services confirmed: not in place.
scenarios.entryPoint: Overbilling, fictitious deliveries or inflated rates are paid.
scenarios.mechanism: Invoices paid without checking approval and receipt are how overbilling and fictitious deliveries get paid. What the answers show: Invoices are paid without being checked against what was approved or received. Quantities checked: not in place. Services confirmed: not in place.
scenarios.concealment: Without three-way match and quantities checked, the activity is processed as routine and nothing records the exception.
scenarios.consequence: Funds paid to a diverted, fictitious or overbilling supplier, often unrecoverable once released. Supplier relationships, payment runs and the supplier master file would need to be investigated and corrected.
warningIndicators: Unauthorised commitments and approval override
Duplicate or false invoices
Overpricing, overbilling and inflated variations
Goods or services paid for but not received
Counterfeit, substituted or substandard goods
Misrepresented supplier credentials

scenarios.title: Supplier payments are diverted through changed bank details

Most changes are verified through the old details or another trusted route. Most executives with a public profile have agreed a verification method with their assistants and finance teams.
